notes: תַּחַת לְ is a compound preposition rendered by the single *under*, so the two morphemes share one unit headed on the governing first morpheme (rules 23, 30); the italicized *is* is the verbless clause's construction-supplied copula joining that prepositional predicate (rules 20, 49), not an addition. The competing reading marking the לְ unrepresented under rule 40 is named in that unit's note.
MACULA's glosses on שְׂמֹאלוֹ and יְמִינוֹ run in reverse (rule 39); each noun takes *left hand* / *right hand* headed on the modifier, since the ASV writes no bare *hand* for any morpheme here.
